title: More high-frequency verbs
intro: A gathering of verbs that are too common to leave out but belong to no single theme. Several are irregular only in the yo form, which is the easiest kind of irregularity to learn.

entries.note: hacer falta is the alternative, built like gustar: me hace falta tiempo.

ex.en: I need to talk to you.

entries.note: See unit 28. utilizar is the more formal of the two.

ex.es: Utilizamos este método desde hace años.
ex.en: We've used this method for years.

entries.en: to pass, to go by; to happen; to spend (time)
entries.note: ¿Qué pasa? is what's happening. pasarlo bien is to have a good time.

ex.es: Pasamos por tu casa camino al centro.
ex.en: We went past your house on the way into town.

ex.es: Pasé el verano en el campo.
ex.en: I spent the summer in the countryside.

entries.note: See unit 1 for quedar without the reflexive.
See unit 2 and unit 10. Paired here because they are the two commonest verbs in any obituary or biography.
See unit 2. creo que and pienso que are interchangeable in most sentences.

ex.en: I don't believe what he says.

entries.en: to go out; to go in
entries.note: See unit 22. Printed on every door: salida and entrada.

ex.es: Salgo del trabajo a las seis.

entries.note: See unit 2 for the three meanings of esperar.

ex.es: Empezamos a las nueve en punto.

entries.en: to finish; to have just done
entries.note: acabar de + infinitive means to have just done something: acabo de llegar, I've just arrived. Extremely common and has no single-word English equivalent.
Spanish has several becomes: hacerse for a chosen change, ponerse for a passing state, volverse for a lasting one, convertirse en for a transformation.

ex.es: Se convirtió en el mejor del equipo.
ex.en: He became the best in the team.

ex.es: Evita la avenida a esta hora.
ex.en: Avoid the avenue at this time.

entries.en: to accept; to deny, to refuse
entries.note: negarse a is to refuse to do something.

ex.en: She accepted the offer straight away.

entries.note: enseñar does the same job in speech — see unit 24.

ex.es: Escoge el que más te guste.
ex.en: Choose the one you like best.

entries.note: se me ocurrió means it occurred to me — an idea rather than an event.

entries.en: to be missing, to be lacking; to be left
entries.note: Built like gustar. falta sal means it needs salt; faltan dos días, there are two days to go.

ex.en: There are ten minutes to go.

entries.en: to be left over, to be more than enough
entries.note: The opposite of faltar. las sobras are leftovers.

ex.en: There was a lot of food left over.

entries.note: vale la pena means it's worth it. In Spain ¡vale! means OK.
